justification: B pairs the Latin text with a matching sans Arabic face, so the Arabic is legible and as large as the English. Its numbered headings span the full width and sit evenly with the Arabic titles. A's Arabic body text is cramped, small and uses a mismatched calligraphic face. A also indents its English column, which leaves the columns unbalanced. B adds running headers and page-of-total folios that help navigation.

A pairs its English and Arabic text at matched sizes and weights, so the bilingual columns sit in balance (A2). B sets its Arabic large and heavy beside small, light grey English, which makes the two columns look uneven and the English harder to read (B2, B3). B's inset navy bands are neat but no clear improvement on A's full-bleed bands. Both charts give the two years the same bar colour and let the legend overlap the bars (A3, B3).

Both share the same navy title band and short single-page layout. B pairs a bold sans heading with a serif body, giving warmer, more readable text and clearer heading weight. A's light 'Memorandum' heading is weaker than its bold 'Key changes' subheading, which inverts the hierarchy. A's thin rule adds little. B's section numbering is slightly unneeded for a memo but harmless.

B uses a calmer, more harmonious serif/Arabic pairing and fuller-width columns, so the bilingual paragraphs sit evenly side by side. A indents its English columns narrowly, which leaves ragged, unbalanced blocks. A's heavy bold sans headings also clash with its Arabic. B's top rule band ties the pages together. A's chart bars in blue are slightly more distinct than B's near-black ones, but overall B reads more cleanly.

A uses larger, more legible table figures and numbered headings, and keeps the notes section intact on its final page. B has small, faint table text and splits the balance sheet after two rows. Its notes are broken across pages, leaving B3 nearly empty with three stranded paragraphs. B's blue cover band is attractive, but it doesn't outweigh the pagination flaws.

A's body text is larger and more legible, and its numbered section headings give a clearer hierarchy. B's body text is small and light. B's single-line title band and divider rule are tidy, but its metadata line is oversized relative to the body, which weakens the hierarchy. A's justified Arabic body reads comfortably, even though its title wraps onto two lines.

A's balance sheet breaks across pages A2 and A3, and its continuation on A3 repeats the header row but has no table title. A1 is a near-empty cover page. B places each statement whole on its own page (B2 balance sheet, B3 cash flow). B's navy header band on B1 combines the cover with content. B's tables are cleanly ruled with a shaded current-period column. A's numbered headings do help navigation slightly, but B's integrity of tables and page use is clearly better.

B sets the body in a larger Arabic face that is easier to read and better proportioned. A's body text is small and light. A keeps the title on one line, while B breaks it awkwardly with one word left alone. Even so, B's more legible body text makes it the more readable page overall. The layouts are otherwise similar.

Design A splits the balance sheet across pages A1–A2, so only the first two rows sit on A1 and the header repeats on A2. It also leaves A3 nearly empty with three short notes stranded there. Design B gives each statement its own page (B1 income, B2 balance sheet, B3 cash flow plus notes) and adds running headers. Its type is larger, though somewhat cramped in the income table.

B sets the Arabic in a more natural naskh-style face, keeps the metadata line compact, and lets the bullets fit on single lines, so it reads more evenly. A's geometric font sits awkwardly with Arabic script, and its metadata wraps clumsily ("٢ / نوفمبر ٢٠٢٥"). A's rule under the header adds little. A's larger text does make it slightly more open. B's section numbering is a mild plus for hierarchy.

A's title band conserves space and its first page is dense and efficient, but its tables use small numerals, and A3 is a nearly empty page carrying only three note lines. B gives up a full page to a sparse cover (B1), yet its tables use larger numerals and fill their pages well (B2, B3). B fits all the notes on B3, adds running headers, and keeps the hierarchy more consistent.

A uses restrained sans headings with numbered sections and compact two-column text, leaving calm whitespace. B's full-bleed dark green bands repeat on every section and dominate the page. They push the narrower text columns into more lines, and the heavy bars break up the reading flow. The tables and charts are essentially equivalent in both designs, so the difference rests on the section treatment.

B uses a refined serif with light rule-topped section heads that pair well with the Arabic and leave calm, even spacing. A stacks three heavy navy banner bands on A2 and another on A3, which crowds the page and outweighs the short paragraphs. A also has awkward justified spacing in the Resolutions list on A3. B's resolution items on B3 read more cleanly, and its chart keeps the legend clear of the bars.

B sets the body in larger type with more generous margins and leading. Its section headings are distinct, and the content fills the page better. A's body text is small and thin, which leaves a large empty lower third. A's meta line is cramped and its bullet glyphs are tiny. B wraps the meta line and some bullets awkwardly, but it is still more comfortable to read overall.

B sets the body text larger and with more even leading, so it reads more easily. Its headings stand clearly above the body text, and the right-aligned blocks share a consistent margin with the rule above. A's body text is small and light, leaving a large empty lower half. A's title band is cleaner on one line, but B's two-line title gives a stronger presence.

A sets the Arabic in a sans face at a size close to the Latin text, so the bilingual columns read evenly. B sets the Arabic noticeably smaller and lighter than the English, which hurts legibility. B's body is also indented under the headings, and the Resolutions list has awkward justified spacing. B's chart bars match colour, so 2024 and 2025 can't be told apart, but A has the same flaw. A's paired columns feel more balanced.

Design A sets each section heading in a heavy full-bleed green band. Three of these stacked on A2, plus one more on A3, make the pages feel blocky and repetitive. Its narrow text columns also break lines awkwardly. Design B uses numbered open headings with wider columns, which gives calmer spacing and smoother reading on B2 and B3. Tables and charts are equivalent in both. Both designs show the same reversed Arabic chart title.

A sets its body text very small and leaves almost half the page empty, and the headings barely stand out. B uses larger, more legible body text with clearer heading weight, and it fills the page more evenly. B's wrapped title and its date line breaking mid-value are minor flaws compared with A's small body text.

A pairs a refined serif with lighter section rules, giving a calm, keepable board document. B's heavy navy bands on every heading dominate the page and compete with the content. B's resolution item 2 is justified with stretched word gaps. A's chart legend overlaps the Q1 2024 bar and hides its label, which costs it a little. B's chart is otherwise equivalent. Overall A reads cleaner.

A uses a dedicated cover with a strong green band heading on page 2. Its table numerals are larger and more legible. The notes section stays intact on A3. B's tables use tiny figures. B also splits the balance sheet awkwardly, leaving only two rows at the bottom of B1. Its notes spill over, so B3 is a mostly empty page with three lines.

A uses strong full-width green section bands with bold bilingual headings, which give clear structure and a confident identity. Its serif body text is larger and easier to read. B is lighter and more refined, but its thin rules and small light-weight body text weaken the hierarchy. The two charts are equivalent: both have the same reversed Arabic chart title, and both have a legend that overlaps the bars. A's justified resolutions text spaces out a little awkwardly, which slightly tempers its lead.

Both designs share the same content, table, and chart, and both have flaws: the chart titles render the Arabic reversed, and in both the 2024 and 2025 bars are the same colour. Design A uses heavy full-bleed green bands for every section heading. On page A2 these dominate the page and cramp the bilingual columns, which become narrow, ragged blocks. Design B uses light rules with bold headings and wider text columns. Its pages feel calmer and more balanced, and its type pairing is more refined. A's bands give a stronger brand presence but feel heavy-handed.

The two designs share the same structure. A sets the text in a naskh-style face that reads more naturally, and its bullets fit on single lines. B uses a geometric Kufi-style face. B's larger size forces awkward wraps: the metadata line breaks before "نوفمبر ٢٠٢٥" and two bullets orphan a single word. This makes B's rhythm choppier.

B pairs a clean sans with a sturdier Arabic face, so the bilingual columns read more evenly. A's Arabic is small and faint beside its serif English. B's dark section bands and running headers give a clearer structure and pace across the pages. B's chart also labels every bar; A's omits the Q1 2024 value. B's Arabic runs somewhat larger than its English, and the bands are heavy, but overall B is easier to read.

A packs content into 6 pages with consistent header and footer bands and balanced pairs of charts per page. B spreads the same content over 8 pages, leaving B4 and B5 mostly empty with a lone chart each. B also has a near-empty cover (B1) and outdented H1s (B3, B8) that look misaligned. B's serif body text is pleasant, but A's rhythm and page fill are stronger. A's Summary heading is light and a bit weak (A2), and its pie labels are oversized (A3).

A uses one cohesive serif family with a ragged-right body, a rule separating the header, and a larger metadata line, which reads calmly. B justifies its short text, leaving visible rivers in the policy paragraph. It also adds numbered headings ('1 Memorandum', '1.1') that are odd for a memo, and its sans/serif mix and tighter spacing feel more cramped. Both leave the lower page empty.

A sets the body in a larger Naskh-style face with comfortable line spacing, so the Arabic text reads more easily. Its header band is heavier, and the title wraps to two lines, but the effect stays dignified. B's body text is small and light, and its metadata line is heavier than the body, which weakens the hierarchy. B's single-line title is tidier, but this does not outweigh the cost to body legibility.

A keeps each statement whole: the balance sheet sits entirely on A2 and the cash flow plus notes on A3. B splits the balance sheet across B2 and B3, breaking the asset section mid-table and repeating the header. B also spends a full page on a sparse cover (B1), and its running header on B2 reads 'قائمة الدخل' though the page carries the balance sheet. A's cover band combined with content on A1 is more efficient, though A3 leaves blank space at the bottom.

B uses larger, more legible table text, numbered section headings, and running headers, and it keeps the notes together on B3. A's small text is harder to read. A also splits the balance sheet after two rows on A1 and leaves three short notes stranded on a nearly empty A3. A's blue header band is a strong opener, but B's cover page is clean and dignified.

A's Naskh-style text face is more legible for Arabic body copy. Its measure is wider, so bullets fit on one line and the page reads compactly. B's geometric Kufi-like face is harder to read at body size, and its narrower text column breaks bullets and the metadata line awkwardly, leaving one-word orphans. B's rule under the header is a nice touch, but A's numbered headings add some structure.

A keeps each statement whole on its own page: the income statement on A1, the balance sheet on A2, and cash flows with notes on A3. B splits the balance sheet across B2 and B3, so readers must flip pages to follow it. B also spends a full mostly-empty dark cover on B1 and leaves the notes stranded on a near-empty B4. A's compact header band and running heads give it a tighter rhythm.

A pairs a sans Latin face with a matched Arabic face at comparable size and weight, so the bilingual columns read as equals (A2, A3). B's Arabic text is noticeably smaller and lighter than its serif English, which unbalances the columns (B2). A's inset navy bands sit within the margins, while B's full-bleed green bands feel heavier. Both charts have the same reversed Arabic title bug, and B's chart legend overlaps the bars (B3).

The two layouts are nearly identical. A uses a traditional Naskh-style Arabic face with clearer letterforms and a darker body text, so it reads more easily. B's geometric light face is thinner and lower in contrast. Its tiny bullet dots and stretched justification also weaken legibility a little. B's title breaks more evenly, but this is minor.

B fits the content into three pages, with the notes sitting right after the cash flow table on B3. A leaves the notes alone on A4, which is mostly empty. B's green title band gives a clear heading on B2, and its single-line column headers make tidier tables. A breaks the balance sheet after just one row on A2, and its table headers wrap. A's rounded Arabic face is pleasant but less formal.

The two layouts are nearly identical. B's Arabic typeface is cleaner and more legible. It bolds the meta labels (إلى، من، التاريخ) and justifies the body paragraph more evenly. A's body text is slightly lighter and less refined. A has a thin rule above the heading that adds some structure. B's numbered section headings are a minor addition. Overall, B reads a bit better.

The two are nearly identical in layout. A uses spurious section numbering (١، ١.١، ١.٢) that clutters the headings. Its justified body text also spreads words awkwardly. B uses ragged, cleaner body text and unnumbered headings, plus a rule that separates the title band from the content, so it reads a little better.

A uses a larger, more commanding title in the navy band and body text at a comfortable reading size that fills the column. B's body text is small and light, and its section headings sit indented inconsistently with the margins, which weakens the hierarchy. B's bright blue band is fine, but its smaller title and smaller text leave the page feeling sparse. A reads more confidently.

The two pages share the same layout. B's serif typesetting is more refined. Its memo header line is set larger than the body, which separates the metadata from the content. Its body text is set ragged and hyphenated, avoiding the stretched justified spacing in A's header line ("To: All staff From: Finance..."). A's sans is clean but feels flatter, and the wide gaps in its justified text hurt readability.

A breaks the balance sheet across pages, leaving only two rows on A2 and repeating the header on A3. B keeps each statement intact, with the balance sheet whole on B2. A's dark full-page cover is striking, and its notes page has generous space. Still, B's compact band header, running heads and complete tables make it easier to read and keep. A4 is mostly empty, while B3 sensibly combines the cash flow statement and the notes.

The two designs are nearly identical in layout. A pairs a sans heading with a serif body, which reads comfortably and gives it a clear heading hierarchy. Its section numbering is slightly odd for a memo. In B, the light-weight 'Memorandum' heading is weaker than the bold 'Key changes' subheading, which inverts the hierarchy. B's light grey sans body also has lower contrast.

A keeps a single consistent left edge: the band title, rule, heading and body all align. B's 'Memorandum' heading hangs out past the indented body, and its rule starts at a different x from the title, which makes the left margin ragged. B also sets the header line larger than the body, an odd jump in scale. A's navy band and its single sans-serif family read more cohesively.

In A, the 'Memorandum' heading hangs to the left of the rule and outside the body column, while the text below is indented, so the left edges misalign. B keeps the heading, rule and body on one consistent left margin. B's justified header line spreads the words loosely, but its alignment reads more coherently overall.

B keeps the balance sheet whole on one page (B2) and gives the cash-flow statement and notes their own page (B3). A splits the balance sheet across A2–A3 and spends a full page on a nearly empty cover (A1). A's body type is slightly cleaner, while B's justified notes stretch their spacing and its title wraps awkwardly (B1, B3). Even so, B's table integrity and steadier page flow make it the better document to read.

B uses a lighter, consistent body size with wider margins and full-width lines, so each bullet fits on a single line and the header line stays intact. A sets heavier, larger text in a narrow column, which wraps the meta line and the bullets awkwardly, and its lower half is crowded. B reads more calmly and evenly, though it leaves more empty space at the bottom.

A pairs a consistent sans heading face with Arabic text that is larger and more legible, and it numbers its sections, which strengthens the hierarchy. B's Arabic body text is small and cramped next to the English and has odd spacing around numerals. B's heavy wide display headings with no numbering read as less refined. The rules and indented columns in B add structure, but they do not offset the readability loss.

B sets the Arabic text in a typeface with better Arabic shaping and weight, so the headings and body read more clearly. B also numbers its sections, which gives clearer hierarchy. A's light geometric face looks thin, and its body text is fainter. The banner and overall layout are nearly identical in both designs.

Design B gives the cover its own page and sets the notes section intact on one page. Its type is larger and more readable. Design A splits the notes awkwardly: one note sits at the bottom of A2 and the remaining three are stranded on a mostly empty A3. A's text is also small and light. B's narrower tables wrap some headers, but overall its pacing is more coherent.

Design A outdents its H1 headings and rules past the text margin on A3 and A8. Its summary and recommendations body is also indented inconsistently, which looks misaligned. Design B keeps every heading on one consistent margin and adds numbered sections and running header/footer bands with page numbers (B2–B8). That gives steadier rhythm and easier navigation. A's headings are somewhat stronger as display type, but overall B is cleaner and more consistent.

B packs content efficiently. It puts the title band and TOC together on B1 and pairs charts on B3, avoiding A's largely empty pages (A1 cover, A2 TOC, A4 and A5 with single charts and large blank space below). A's serif body text and indented Summary/Recommendations sections are refined, though inconsistent with the headings. B's heavy header and footer bands are somewhat heavy, but give consistent navigation. B's Summary heading is light-weight and inconsistent.

A uses a refined serif with a matched Arabic face and quiet rule-led section heads, so the bilingual columns sit in calm balance (A2, A3). B's heavy full-bleed green bands repeat three times on one page and dominate the content (B2, B3). B's larger, heavier text makes the English columns feel cramped, and its Resolutions list shows awkward justified gaps (B3). Charts and tables are essentially the same in both.

A pairs a mismatched display sans with a delicate serif, and its section heads read as consistent, quiet rules that keep the page calm. B's full-bleed green bands give stronger section hierarchy and a consistent rhythm, adding running headers on each page. However, the heavy bands dominate the short sections. In A, the indented English columns leave an awkward left gap. Overall, B is more navigable and finished.

B's bold numbered section headings with running headers and 'Page x of 3' footers give stronger hierarchy and navigation. Its Arabic and Latin body text is more evenly matched in weight. A's light, thin headings with rules feel weaker, and its decorative top band adds little. B's justified Resolutions text shows some wide word spacing, but its overall structure is clearer.

Design B uses a serif body text with clean, numbered section headings that read calmly and match the bilingual columns well. Design A repeats heavy navy banner bars for every section and adds a dark header band, so its short pages feel heavy. In A3 the chart legend overlaps the bars, while in B3 the legend sits clear of the data. A has slightly stronger visual punch, but B is lighter and easier to read.

A keeps the notes section whole on its own page (A4). B splits the notes: the heading and note 1 end page B2, and the rest spills onto a near-empty B3. B's text also shows rendering glitches ("متجر؟") and very small type. A's dark cover and consistent page headers give a cleaner structure. B's blue band is attractive, but the table pages are otherwise similar.

A keeps each statement whole on its own page, with a strong navy title band that opens the document. B leaves most of its cover page empty. It then splits the balance sheet across B2 and B3, so readers have to re-read the repeated header to follow it. A's notes page has empty space at the bottom (A3), but its tables stay intact and easier to follow.

A uses bold, numbered section heads in a sans face that stand out clearly over the serif body. Its Arabic is set in a consistent, legible naskh-style face, and its running headers include section names. B has light, unnumbered heads and a more decorative Arabic face mixed with a small, light serif, which weakens hierarchy and legibility. Both designs use nearly identical tables and charts, and B's rules over the headings are a minor plus.

The two layouts are nearly identical. B uses a more traditional Naskh-style Arabic face that reads more comfortably at body size. Its bullets are solid dots, which are clearer than A's tiny dots. A's geometric font is lighter, and its justified paragraph stretches word spacing. B's title line-break leaves a single orphaned word, but this is minor.

A has a strong green cover and a full-width green title band on page 2 that anchors the document, with single-line table headers. B's cover is plain, its title wraps awkwardly to a second line with a stray year, and its column header "الربع الثالث ٢٠٢٥" breaks onto two lines. Both use mixed Latin section numbers. The tables are otherwise near-identical.

A uses heavier, darker headings with section numbers, so the subsections stand out clearly. B's light-weight heading font gives weaker contrast between headings and body text. The thin rule in B adds little. A's body text also reads more crisply.

A combines the cover and table of contents on one page and pairs Channel Mix with Device Share on a single page. The result is six evenly filled pages. B gives the title its own mostly blank cover (B1) and leaves B4 and B5 each holding a single chart above half-empty space, so the pacing feels padded. Both use the same charts, table and header bands. B's numbered headings and serif body text are pleasant, but A's density and page balance are better.

Design A keeps a consistent left margin, so the rule, headings and body all align. In B, the 'Memorandum' heading and the rule hang outside the text column while the body is indented. B's justified body text also opens uneven word gaps. A's serif pairing reads more coherently. Both leave a large empty lower half.

A pairs a serif body with a sans heading and keeps the Arabic and Latin columns at matched sizes. Its section headings are clean and numbered. In B, the heavy navy banner for every section dominates the page, and the Arabic body runs visibly larger and heavier than the light English text, which unbalances the bilingual columns. B's chart also has a legend overlapping the bars. Both share the same table and chart issues (the chart title's Arabic is reversed), but A reads calmer and more consistent.

A fits the content on three pages with a strong green title band. Its tables use wider columns, so the headers sit on one line. B wraps the cover title and the page-2 headline awkwardly, breaks table headers onto two lines, and wraps the cash-flow row labels. It also strands the short notes alone on a mostly empty fourth page.

B's Naskh-style text face reads more naturally for Arabic body copy. Its bullets and steps each fit on a single line, giving a calmer rhythm. A's geometric Kufi-like face is wider, so bullets wrap awkwardly and the date line breaks onto a second line. Headers and layout are otherwise equivalent.

B is the better design. It packs the same content into 6 pages by pairing charts (B3, B4, B5), while A leaves large empty areas on A4 and A5, each holding a single small chart. A also spends a whole nearly empty cover page (A1). B's banded cover with the TOC (B1) and the Recommendations band (B6) add structure. B's light, loosely tracked sans body text is a bit less readable than A's serif, and the unnumbered, thin 'Summary' heading weakens its hierarchy slightly. On balance, B's denser and more even pacing wins.

B sets the body text larger and justified, with clearer, bolder section headings. Its body text fills the width more evenly. A uses small, light body text and a thin rule, and the content sits narrowly and looks sparse. B's two-line title wraps awkwardly and its headings carry odd section numbering, but overall B reads more comfortably.

B packs the content into three pages. Its table headers sit on one line ("تسعة أشهر ٢٠٢٥" does not wrap), and its numbered section headings and running headers make navigation easier. A wraps its column headers and splits the balance sheet after only one row. It also leaves the notes stranded on a mostly empty fourth page with wide justified gaps. A's dark cover is striking, but B's interior pages flow better.

B keeps every element on one consistent left edge under the header band. A's 'Memorandum' heading hangs outdented at the far left while the body sits indented, and a stray rule floats out of line, which makes the alignment look broken. A's header-line text is also oversized relative to its body text. B's numbered headings are a little bureaucratic, but its spacing and alignment are cleaner.

The content and charts are the same in both. A holds a consistent left margin, and its numbered headings give clear structure in the TOC and body. B pushes its H1s (Summary, Recommendations) out into the left margin and indents the body text that follows, so the text edge is ragged and inconsistent (B3, B8). A's header and footer bands frame each page steadily. B's footers are lighter but its running heads are inconsistent. B's cover places the title lower, off-centre and left-aligned, which works, but it does not offset the misaligned body.

A sets its Arabic text at a size and weight that match the Latin, so the bilingual columns read as equals. In B the Arabic body text is markedly smaller and spindly next to the serif English, which hurts readability (B2, B3). A's dark heading bands and running headers give a clear structure (A2, A3). B's rule-line headings are lighter and elegant, but the columns are unevenly weighted. The charts are comparable; both show the same reversed Arabic chart title.

The tables are essentially identical in both designs. B's full-bleed green cover and green title band on page 2 give the document a stronger, more deliberate identity. In B the main title fits on a single line inside the band. A's plain white cover is sparse and its title wraps awkwardly onto a second line. B's Arabic body text also sets more evenly, while A uses tracked justification in the notes. Section numbering in A helps a little, but overall B reads as more polished.

A keeps a single consistent left edge for the heading and the body, and its navy band sits calmly with the text. B's 'Memorandum' heading hangs far left of an indented body, and a rule runs out to the left margin. Together these break the alignment. B's header line is also set larger than its body text, which makes the type sizes uneven. A's section numbering is slightly bureaucratic but tidy.

A gives each statement its own page: the balance sheet stays whole on A2, and the cash flow statement and notes sit together on A3. Its body type is larger and readable. B splits the balance sheet across B1 and B2 and repeats the table header. It also splits the notes, leaving three short lines alone on a nearly empty B3. B's text is small, with odd glyphs in the notes.

B keeps one consistent left edge for the heading, rule and body, and its ragged-right body text reads smoothly. A's "Memorandum" heading hangs outside the indented body column, and its justified text opens rivers of space. A's sans/serif pairing and vivid blue band are bolder but less cohesive. Both designs leave the lower half of the page empty.

A fits the content into three pages. Its statements are compact, with numbered section headings and wide label columns that keep cash-flow rows on one line (A3). B splits the balance sheet across pages after only one asset row (B2), wraps column headers and cash-flow labels (B3), and leaves a mostly empty final page holding only the notes (B4). B's dark cover is striking, but the light geometric Arabic face is less readable for dense figures.

A sets the body at a comfortable size with generous line spacing, and its content fills the page well beneath a dark header band. B's body text is very small and thin, which makes the Arabic hard to read. It also leaves a large empty lower third. B's misaligned title-to-meta sizes give weaker hierarchy, though its single-line title is neat.

A's serif setting uses a ragged right margin and gives the To/From/Date/Re header line larger type, which sets it apart from the body. B justifies its text, so the To/From line and the body show uneven, stretched word spacing. B's header line is also the same size as the body, which flattens the hierarchy. B's spacing is tighter and more cramped. Both designs have the same header band and leave the same large empty area below the text.

B uses a refined serif throughout. Its header block is set larger, it is ragged-right, and the bullets are generously spaced. A justifies its short lines, which opens visible gaps in the header line and the body. A's numbered headings ('1 Memorandum', '1.1') are odd in a memo. B's body text is a bit small and its 'Memorandum' heading is light, but overall B reads more cleanly.
